results.text:
I couldn't get this deck accepted by `submit_deck`, so it is not submitted and has no label. The validator rejected your unchanged main deck twice. Both times the error was "Outside the requested colors (UB): Tamiyo, Inquisitive Student // Tamiyo, Seasoned Scholar". Tamiyo costs {U}, and the archetype data shows it in 53.5% of Dimir Tempo lists. I suspect the check trips on her −3 text, which mentions a green card. I haven't confirmed that. I kept your main exactly as given rather than cut four Tamiyo to get past the check. `check_deck` returned ok with no errors or warnings for the 60 plus this 15.

**The plan:** Your main is the usual Dimir Tempo shell. It runs cheap threats and disruption (Tamiyo, Bowmasters, Borrower, Murktide), backed by Daze, Force of Will, Wasteland and Thoughtseize. The sideboard keeps that plan and adds hate cards for the matchups the meta data says you will meet.

**Sideboard (15):**
- 2 Massacre
- 2 Surgical Extraction
- 2 Consign to Memory
- 2 Force of Negation
- 2 Hydroblast
- 1 Damping Sphere
- 1 Nihil Spellbomb
- 1 Barrowgoyf
- 1 Dauthi Voidwalker
- 1 Sheoldred's Edict

**Why these cards.** The tools show the shares and card text. Which cards are good in which matchup is my judgment.
- **Massacre** (2): Ocelot Aggro is the second-biggest deck at 9.0%, and it plays Plains, Guide of Souls, Ocelot Pride, Voice of Victory and Ajani. Massacre is free if the opponent has a Plains and you have a Swamp. Your Underground Sea and Swamp count as Swamps. It also covers Death and Taxes (3.5%). It hurts your own Bowmasters and Tamiyo, so keep it out against decks without small creatures.
- **Surgical Extraction** (2): It hits Ocelot Pride, and it works against Reanimator, Hogaak and Doomsday. It costs 2 life if you have no black mana. 57.1% of Ocelot lists board it themselves, so expect them to have it too.
- **Consign to Memory** (2): It counters colorless spells and triggered abilities. That covers Tron and Eldrazi Aggro, whose creatures are colorless. It also answers Blink, OmniTell and Sneak and Show triggers, and Ocelot Pride triggers.
- **Force of Negation** (2): It counters noncreature spells, and the free mode works on the opponent's turn. It is good against Tron (7.1%), Doomsday (5.8%), The Epic Storm and Beanstalk Control. 94.5% of Dimir Tempo lists board it.
- **Hydroblast** (2): It answers red spells and permanents. Targets include Izzet Tempo (4.6%), and Goblin Bombardment, Amped Raptor and Phlage in Ocelot Aggro. 71.4% of Dimir Tempo lists board it. The text only names red, so it does nothing in the Dimir mirror.
- **Damping Sphere** (1): It slows Tron, which is 7.1% of the meta, and Lands (5.1%). It also taxes storm turns from Sewer Combo and The Epic Storm.
- **Nihil Spellbomb** (1): A cheap graveyard answer for Reanimator and Hogaak. It draws a card if you pay {B} when it is put into a graveyard from the battlefield.
- **Dauthi Voidwalker** (1): It has shadow, so it attacks past blockers. It also exiles opposing cards that would go to the graveyard, which hurts Reanimator. Be careful: Doomsday lists run it too, so it can be a target for their removal.
- **Barrowgoyf** (1): A deathtouch, lifelink threat. Use it against Ocelot Aggro and midrange decks, where lifelink and a sturdy body matter. It is already in 72.2% of Dimir Tempo sideboards.
- **Sheoldred's Edict** (1): A flexible removal spell against big creatures such as Eldrazi, Blink and Reanimator targets. It also hits planeswalkers.

I left out Toxic Deluge, Null Rod and Grafdigger's Cage. Deluge fights your own creature plan. Null Rod and Cage only matter against a few decks, and Spellbomb and Surgical already cover the graveyard decks.

**Mana.** I changed no lands, so there are 19 lands. The 5,000-game simulation of the main deck gave these numbers:
- Mulligan rate: 8.7%.
- Colored mana available on time: 69.3% on turn 1, 86.5% on turn 2, 87.6% on turn 3.
- Screw rate: 29.2%.
- Flood rate: 0.2%.

These match the numbers the simulator reported for the archetype's reference list. `check_deck` suggests 20.2 lands and counts 15 blue and 13 black sources. The real Dimir Tempo lists average 18.94 lands, so I judged 19 acceptable. The simulation counts only land drops and colors, not cantrips like Brainstorm and Ponder.

**Sideboarding (judgment, not measured):**
- **Ocelot Aggro, Death and Taxes:** Bring in 2 Massacre, 2 Surgical Extraction, 2 Hydroblast and Barrowgoyf. Take out Daze and some Thoughtseize.
- **Tron, Eldrazi:** Bring in 2 Consign to Memory, 2 Force of Negation, Damping Sphere and Edict. Take out Fatal Push and the weaker threats.
- **Izzet Tempo:** Bring in 2 Hydroblast and Consign to Memory. Add Edict if they have bigger creatures.
- **Doomsday, Storm, combo:** Bring in 2 Force of Negation, Damping Sphere and Dauthi Voidwalker. Take out slow or creature-only removal.
- **Reanimator, Hogaak:** Bring in Surgical Extraction, Nihil Spellbomb, Dauthi Voidwalker and Edict.
- **Blink, OmniTell, Sneak and Show:** Bring in 2 Consign to Memory, 2 Force of Negation and Hydroblast. Surgical Extraction can hit their key creature.
- **Dimir mirror:** Bring in Barrowgoyf and Edict. Hydroblast does nothing here. Massacre only helps if their creatures are small and yours are few.

This is a tuned sideboard built on the Dimir Tempo archetype's real sideboard data, with the main deck left alone. Which cards go in and out against each deck is my judgment, not tested.

results.prompt: Combine Living End and Scam into one Modern deck.
results.text:
I couldn't lock the engine. `submit_engine` rejected both attempts with "The player named Scam; it must be part of the engine."

"Scam" isn't a card. A card search for "scam" returned nothing, and no tag by that name exists. It's the name of an archetype, so I didn't enter a made-up card to get past the check. Grief and Fury, the core of Scam, are banned in Modern (`card_info`).

The plan is the one I submitted:
- **Cascade engine:** 4 Living End, 4 Shardless Agent, 4 Violent Outburst and 4 Demonic Dread, aiming to cast Living End by turn 3.
- **Scam half:** 4 Subtlety and 4 Endurance. These are the legal evoke Elementals, and each one evoked or discarded is a creature in the graveyard for Living End to return.
- **Graveyard fodder:** 4 Street Wraith, 3 Striped Riverwinder and 2 Waker of Waves, which can be cycled or discarded.
- **Undying Evil:** 1 copy, as the trick. At 1 mana it is a blank cascade hit, so I'd keep it to that one copy.
- **Odds:** 12 cascade spells give an 88.7% chance of seeing at least one by turn 3 on the play (`draw_odds`, 9 cards seen). Adding 20 fodder cards, seeing at least one of each group is 86.9%.

To go on, I need either a ruling that this Scam-style package counts as "Scam", or a card name or spelling for "Scam" that the tools recognise.

results.prompt: Build a Commander deck with Atraxa, Praetors' Voice that's all about proliferate.
results.text:
The deck is built and passes `check_deck`, but `submit_deck` did not accept it, so it is not formally submitted.

**Why the submission failed.** The locked plan requires Atraxa in the main deck, but Commander rules put her in the command zone. Every variant I tried failed one check:
- Atraxa as commander with 99 other cards: rejected because the plan wants her in the main deck.
- Atraxa in the main deck with no commander field: rejected with "Commander needs a commander."
- Atraxa in both places: rejected as 101 cards with 2 copies of Atraxa.

The legal build is below. `check_deck` returned no errors for it: Atraxa in the command zone plus 99 other cards.

**Plan.** Land Atraxa on turn 4 and proliferate every end step. Cheap proliferate pieces such as Evolution Sage, Flux Channeler, Metastatic Evangel and Ezuri add more triggers. Tekuthal doubles all of them. Counter doublers (Winding Constrictor, Hardened Scales, Corpsejack Menace, Branching Evolution, Doubling Season, Vorinclex) and planeswalkers turn that into big creatures and loyalty. Finishers are combat, Scheming Aspirant drain, Vraska's −9 and Agent Frank Horrigan's double proliferate.

**The 99 (plus Atraxa as commander):**
- **Locked engine (28 cards plus Karn's Bastion):** all at 1 copy, as specified.
- **Ramp, 9 cards:** Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Chromatic Lantern, Birds of Paradise, Cultivate, Kodama's Reach, Farseek, Nature's Lore, Three Visits. Several of these fetch basics or Forest-typed duals, which also trigger Evolution Sage's landfall.
- **Draw, 3 cards:** Rhystic Study, Sylvan Library, Harmonize.
- **Interaction, 8 cards:** Swords to Plowshares, Vindicate, Utter End, Beast Within, Generous Gift, Cyclonic Rift, Toxic Deluge, Heroic Intervention.
- **Extra proliferate payoffs and sources, 8 cards:** Contentious Plan, Experimental Augury, Tromell, Thrummingbird, Agent Frank Horrigan, Norn's Choirmaster, Tidus, Cankerbloom.
- **Counter makers, 7 cards:** Walking Ballista, Hangarback Walker, Branching Evolution, Oko, Nissa Who Shakes the World, Tamiyo Field Researcher, Sword of Truth and Justice.
- **Lands, 36 including Karn's Bastion:**
  - Command Tower and Exotic Orchard.
  - 6 shock lands.
  - 4 triomes.
  - 6 fetch lands.
  - 6 "enters tapped unless you control two basics" duals (Sunken Hollow, Prairie Stream, Canopy Vista, Vernal Fen, Sodden Verdure, Eclipsed Steppe).
  - 4 Forest, 3 Island, 2 Swamp, 2 Plains.

**Mana.** Measured in `check_deck`: 36 lands, average mana value 3.05. The version with 17 basics had about 14.5 W, 15.5 U, 15.5 B and 17.5 G sources. The final build adds the six dual lands, so colored sources are higher. The final `check_deck`, run with Atraxa duplicated in the main, shows 16.5 W, 17.5 U, 16.5 B and 18.5 G.
- **Warnings:** it still warns that Tekuthal, Harmonize, Cathars' Crusade and Yawgmoth want more sources than a four-color deck can give. That is the cost of the four colors Atraxa requires.
- **Simulation:** I ran 5,000 games on the basic-land version. 21.7% were mulligans, and all four colors were available by turn 4 in 69.8% of games. With the six dual lands swapped in, that rose to 74.9% on turn 4 (77.1% by turn 6). Those runs do not count ramp spells or fetch lands, so real consistency is likely better.
- **Engine readiness:** on the final list, 40.4% of games had a proliferate-enabler or counter-doubler card in hand by turn 6, and 28.2% had one castable by then.

**Sideboarding.** Commander has no sideboard. Swap these slots for the matchup:
- **Against fast combo:** the deck's cheap interaction (Swords, Cyclonic Rift, Heroic Intervention) is the answer.
- **Against creature decks:** Toxic Deluge is the only sweeper. Use it before you commit your own creatures.
- **Against counter hate (Vorinclex, Hex Parasite):** Vindicate, Utter End and Beast Within answer it. Cankerbloom can also destroy an artifact or enchantment.
- **Against sweepers:** the planeswalkers, Hangarback Walker and Heroic Intervention give some resilience.

**Label and donor.** This is a brew. No proliferate or Atraxa reference list exists in the tool (`archetype` and `reference_list` returned nothing, and there is no Commander meta data). I could not borrow a real shell. The mana base, ramp and interaction are my own judgment, modeled on standard four-color Commander builds.

**Unverified.** Win rates and speed against real opponents. The claim that Atraxa lands on turn 4 comes from her mana cost, not a simulation.

engine.thesis: Atraxa proliferates every end step while a wide set of repeatable and one-shot proliferate effects, counter doublers, and counter-generating planeswalkers and creatures snowball +1/+1, loyalty, and poison counters. Four colors (G/W/U/B) are forced by Atraxa's identity and let the deck use the best proliferate cards in all of them.
engine.winCondition: Grow a board of creatures with +1/+1 counters (Atraxa, Contaminator, Corpsejack/Constrictor-boosted bodies) and planeswalkers with loyalty counters, using proliferate (doubled by Tekuthal) to push counters out of reach; finish through combat, Scheming Aspirant drain, or poison from proliferating.

Decks that do not remove a single key threat quickly
Board stalls, since counters grow the board each turn
losesTo: Fast combo / cEDH-style decks (no tournament data was available for Commander to confirm speed)
Counter-hate such as Hex Parasite or Vorinclex effects held by opponents
Early removal on Atraxa before the first end step
